invariants.title: Authoritative structure
invariants.trigger: The change classifies, filters, authorizes, or otherwise decides over values whose complete vocabulary is not fixed by an owned protocol.
invariants.requiredStructure: Derive the decision from an authoritative typed value, explicit state, provider result, or positive protocol grammar. Literal tables and pattern sets are valid only when the owning contract closes and versions the domain.
invariants.prohibitedFailure: Do not infer open-world meaning from partial keywords, names, paths, messages, or an expanding exception list.
invariants.evidence: Exercise valid previously unseen values, invalid structured states, and the authoritative boundary that makes the decision.

invariants.title: Single policy authority
invariants.trigger: One rule, vocabulary, or compatibility decision is consumed by more than one runtime, schema, template, generated artifact, or repository.
invariants.requiredStructure: Assign one authoritative owner. Generate derived copies or prove their parity, and version immutable consumer-facing policy where independent release timing exists.
invariants.prohibitedFailure: Do not maintain hand-synchronized semantic copies that can drift while each copy remains locally valid.
invariants.evidence: Identify the owner and prove generation, parity, hash locking, or compatibility against every derived consumer surface.

invariants.title: Bounded side effects
invariants.trigger: The change introduces or materially changes a resource-bearing or privileged side effect whose failure, lifetime, cleanup, retry, or platform behavior can escape the local operation.
invariants.requiredStructure: Define explicit scope, resource and time bounds, cancellation and failure behavior, cleanup ownership, and the least authority needed; isolate platform-specific or privileged behavior behind a narrow boundary.
invariants.prohibitedFailure: Do not allow unbounded work, broad cleanup, ambient authority, swallowed failure, or a silent fallback that weakens the claimed guarantee.
invariants.evidence: Exercise success, boundary exhaustion, interruption, failure propagation, cleanup scope, and platform adapters that the change affects.

invariants.title: Contractual evolution
invariants.trigger: The change alters a released, persisted, externally consumed, or independently versioned format, API, CLI, package contract, protocol, schema, platform promise, migration, or recovery path.
invariants.requiredStructure: State compatibility and migration behavior explicitly. Version immutable contracts, preserve supported readers and writers, or declare and verify an intentional breaking boundary and recovery path.
invariants.prohibitedFailure: Do not mutate a released contract implicitly, rely on an undocumented migration, or claim compatibility from current-version tests alone.
invariants.evidence: Exercise supported old and new fixtures, installed artifacts, failure and recovery behavior, and every claimed platform or compatibility boundary.

invariants.title: Evidence-bound assurance
invariants.trigger: The change or release claims correctness, security, compatibility, readiness, completion, or production suitability.
invariants.requiredStructure: Bind objective checks to the exact unchanged candidate and require independent judgment for contextual properties. Keep consumer-owned verification and enforced readiness capabilities as the authority for production claims.
invariants.prohibitedFailure: Do not substitute prose, a checklist, self-review, stale output, an unverified build, or an invariant assessment itself for current evidence.
invariants.evidence: Record passing consumer-owned profiles on one snapshot, independent review of that snapshot, and artifact or platform evidence required by the affected readiness capabilities.
